subject: Renewal review: rightsizing + feature-driven expansion (Q3 plan)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@palmetto.health>, ops@palmetto.health
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-30T17:15:00Z
Subject: Renewal review: rightsizing + feature-driven expansion (Q3 plan)

Hi Alyssa —

Quick note ahead of our renewal window: I pulled a short usage & performance recap for Palmetto through the end of June (attached) and sketched two optional paths for Q3: a rightsizing adjustment to match your new inference mix, or an expansion that pairs a modest commit increase with the new Moderation + Retrieval add-on we discussed.

Highlights from the attached report:
- Overall token consumption is +28% QoQ driven by embedding-heavy batch jobs (peak windows 03:00–05:00 UTC).
- Generation latency is stable, but KV-cache hit rate drops on longer conversations — explains some CPU spikes.
- Current plan utilization: 76% of reserved throughput; burst events have hit soft limits three times in last 60 days.

Suggested next steps (proposed call next week):
1) Review a rightsizing plan that reduces over-provisioned reserved GPU hours and adds a small burst buffer (recommended: move 15% of static capacity to burstable).
2) Evaluate a targeted upsell: +20% commit for predictable throughput and include Retrieval package for 90-day pilot (ROI model attached).
3) Confirm any security/compliance constraints for on-prem ingestion if you decide to increase embedding throughput.

Attachments: Palmetto_Q1-Q2_usage_report.pdf; Palmetto_ROI_model_Q3.xlsx

If you share availability Ill lock in a 30-min slot and bring Ben and Sean to walk the ops/finance tradeoffs.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Palmetto_Q1-Q2_usage_report.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: Palmetto_ROI_model_Q3.xlsx (Excel, 230KB)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@palmetto.health>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-31T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal review: rightsizing + feature-driven expansion (Q3 plan)

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments — helpful. A few quick clarifications before we schedule:

1) Embeddings: that +28% sounds right — we had a new personalization job go live in mid-May. Can you break down the embedding token spend by job (batch vs. real-time)? Were particularly sensitive to costs tied to offline recompute.

2) Latency/throughput: the KV-cache comment worries our infra team. Is the cache hit variability something you can mitigate without doubling commit?

3) Pricing: the ROI file looks promising. Any chance of a temporary burst-credit during the re-index window (we have a heavy re-ingestion planned in August)?

If you can respond to 1–3 I can align with procurement on timing.

Best,

Alyssa Chen
Director, Platform Ops
Palmetto Health
[ops@palmetto.health]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@palmetto.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T14:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal review: rightsizing + feature-driven expansion (Q3 plan)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the fast reply. Answers inline and a short plan below.

1) Embeddings breakdown:
- Batch recompute (daily): ~64% of embedding tokens — large jobs scheduled off-peak (2–6am UTC).
- Real-time personalization: ~36% — unpredictable but lower per-job token volume.
Well attach a job-level ledger in the drive folder; for the short term we recommend throttling non-critical recompute windows and moving some batch jobs to the weekend to smooth charges. (See Palmetto_ROI_model_Q3.xlsx tab "JobBreakdown").

2) KV-cache variability:
- Root cause: long conversation lengths with mixed model variants reduces effective cache reuse.
- Mitigation: enable selective prefix caching and pad lower-priority conversations into a separate worker pool (no change to commit). This reduces CPU spikes without increasing baseline commit. Sean can run a small experiment (7 days) and share before/after metrics.

3) Burst-credit for August re-index: we can offer a one-time burst credit equivalent to 150k tokens during the re-ingest window, plus an option for short-term capacity lift at a reduced overage rate. Ill confirm the credit in writing once Ben signs off.

Proposed plan (we can discuss on a 30-min call):
- Option A (Rightsize): reduce reserved baseline 15%, add 25% burstable capacity and the selective caching config. Expected cost impact: neutral in Q3, improved latency variance.
- Option B (Expand + Pilot): +20% commit for sustained throughput, include 90-day Retrieval pilot, provide August 150k token burst-credit, and 10% pilot discount on Retrieval seats. Expected ROI: faster personalization responses, lower downstream compute due to retrieval efficiency (see ROI model).

Ive attached the ROI model and a draft SOW for the pilot. If this looks good Ben can confirm the burst-credit and Ill route the SOW to DocuSign.

Thanks — Tessa

[Attachment: Palmetto_ROI_model_Q3.xlsx (Excel, 230KB)]
[Attachment: Palmetto_SOW_draft_v5.docx (DOCX, 120KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-03T14:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal review: rightsizing + feature-driven expansion (Q3 plan)

Hi Alyssa —

Ben here — quick operational note: weve approved the one-time August burst credit of 150,000 tokens and will extend a temporary overage rate of 0.6x for any additional capacity during the re-index window. We can move forward with Option B pilot economics as Tessa outlined: 20% commit increase + 90-day Retrieval pilot at a 10% pilot discount.

Next steps:
- Ill ask Legal to finalize the SOW; expect DocuSign link within 48 hours.
- Sean will run the 7-day selective-caching experiment and share a short readout before the pilot starts.
- Tessa will schedule a kickoff call and add a billing note for the August burst credit.

Happy to chat if you want to walk the numbers; otherwise well route the SOW and lock the kickoff.

Best regards,

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference
